children: Nomura remains watchful on rural demand amid a wider-than-expected monsoon deficit and strengthening El Niño conditions, but continues to favour consumer companies with higher urban saliency, pricing power and strong brands. Its top picks are Marico (MRCO IN, Buy) and Tata Consumer (TATACONS IN, Buy) in consumer staples, and Titan (TTAN IN, Buy) and United Spirits (UNITDSPR IN, Buy) in consumer discretionary.

"We remain watchful on rural demand as we believe that it will likely face multiple headwinds of below-normal monsoon, El Niño, and product price increases being taken by companies due to the West-Asia conflict," Nomura said.

The brokerage said overall inflation and mid-single-digit price increases remain manageable for now, but further product price hikes and any impact on agricultural yields could add pressure on demand and consumption. It also flagged potential moderation in winter portfolios such as cold creams, lotions and Chyawanprash due to warmer winters.

Rainfall in August, which accounts for around 30% of the season's rainfall, was 16% below normal across many parts of the country. Rainfall between June and August was around 14% below normal, against the full-season forecast of 10% below normal. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) expects September rainfall to also be below normal at less than 91% of the long-period average.
Despite the weak monsoon, the Kharif sowing deficit narrowed sharply to 1.5% year-on-year as of August 20 from 23% as of June 25. Rice sowing, however, remained down 3.2%.

Nomura said high government rice and wheat stocks could help keep inflation in check. As of August 1, rice stocks were around three times the buffer norm, while wheat stocks were around 1.8 times the buffer norm.

The brokerage also flagged strengthening El Niño conditions. "Moderate to strong El Niño conditions are prevailing (vs earlier expectation of moderate El Niño) and could strengthen gradually to develop into strong El Niño conditions by September," Nomura said.
A potential shift to a positive Indian Ocean Dipole could provide some respite, although Nomura noted uncertainty around its timing and strength.

title: Nomura flags rural demand risks as monsoon deficit widens; Marico, Titan among top picks
